references.observed: Complete historic seaward front actually inspected: warm ochre/pale stone facade, two cylindrical end towers with steep slate conical/curved roofs and open top lanterns, a long steep main hip/mansard roof with dormers, a central shaped clock gable, repeated rectangular and tall arched windows, pilasters/cornices and open balcony rails. Three broad glazed arched ground entrances lie between narrower end arches. The narrow strip of quay and rock seawall is context, not part of the passenger building. Exact inscriptions, railway logo, sculptural reliefs and banners are not copied.

2024 whole front/long-side view actually inspected. Steep gray slate main roof and corner conical roofs/lanterns are visible during scaffolding/restoration. A long side wing has repeated arched ground openings, several upper window levels and a dense row of small roof dormers, with larger shaped roof gables near its ends. The source model should represent the complete permanent architectural exterior; temporary scaffolding, perimeter banners/fences and the large roof logo are excluded. Hidden courtyard/rear opening inventory remains approximate.

Q800973 and retained way/473151877 identify the historic U-shaped station passenger building. Current full principal component 35184845240709 (index45) and its two tile-edge fragments (indices28/29) share the same encoded identity and match the twin seaward towers and unequal rear wings. The small seaward strip building, quays, railway structures and independent rear buildings remain separate. Encoded IDs are not asserted to be OSM element IDs. Native 7.25m height conflicts with the clearly multi-story photographed architecture; preserve it as a conflicting map fact, not a source building height.
